items.stem: Which change most directly reduces the per-request cost of an LLM call?

options.text: Reducing the number of input and output tokens
options.rationale: Correct: cost scales with tokens, so fewer tokens means lower cost.
Temperature affects randomness, not token-based cost.
More context adds tokens and raises cost.
That has no effect on cost.

items.explanation: Correct: cost scales with tokens, so fewer tokens means lower cost.

items.stem: Which TWO techniques can cut cost while keeping quality acceptable for many requests? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Caching responses to repeated or identical queries
options.rationale: Correct: caching avoids paying for the same answer twice.

options.text: Routing easy requests to a smaller, cheaper model
options.rationale: Correct: a cascade sends simple cases to a cheaper model.

options.text: Always using the largest available model
options.rationale: That maximises cost rather than reducing it.

options.text: Doubling the retrieved context on every call

items.explanation: Correct: caching avoids paying for the same answer twice.

items.stem: Before aggressively cutting cost, what should a team define to avoid silent quality loss?

options.text: A measurable quality floor the optimised system must stay above
options.rationale: Correct: a quality floor ensures cost cuts do not degrade answers unnoticed.
Temperature is not a quality guarantee.
Context length is not a quality floor.
